papers.title: Mapping a genome-scale in vivo knockout screen to a mechanistic network model identifies VAV2, RASA1, and LEPR as regulators of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
papers.abstract: Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy is a leading clinical predictor of heart failure, yet newly identified candidate genes often remain disconnected from the signaling mechanisms that govern cardiomyocyte growth. We developed a computational-experimental pipeline that integrates genome-scale mouse knockout phenotypes with a logic-based differential equation model of hypertrophic signaling. Among 9,605 genes evaluated by the International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium, 939 knockout lines induced abnormal heart morphology. Directional curation of hypertrophy-related sub-phenotypes followed by interaction-b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors integrated genome-scale mouse knockout phenotype data from the International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium with a logic-based differential equation model of hypertrophic signaling to connect candidate genes to mechanisms of cardiomyocyte growth. Among 9,605 genes screened, 939 knockout lines showed abnormal heart morphology, and the network mapping identified VAV2, RASA1, and LEPR as regulators of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. This demonstrates a computational-experimental pipeline for linking large-scale in vivo genetic screens to mechanistic signaling models.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, built using a new reconstruction approach that incorporates experimentally determined nutrient requirements. They also characterize the strain's secretions, providing a more accurate framework for studying its metabolism in controlled in vitro conditions. This fills a gap left by previous automatically generated draft models with limited functional accuracy.

papers.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal temporal tra
papers.summary: This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis reveals dynamic regulatory transitions during injury and identifies candidate genes with renoprotective potential. The work provides a temporal map of molecular events underlying cisplatin nephrotoxicity and regeneration.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals autophagy-associated transcriptional vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons after atrazine exposure.
papers.abstract: Atrazine (ATZ) is a widely used triazine herbicide with potential neurotoxic effects, but the cell-type-specific responses of midbrain dopaminergic neurons to ATZ exposure remain poorly defined. In this study, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing to midbrain tissues from adult male mice exposed to ATZ for 28 days (a sub-acute exposure) to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with dopaminergic neuronal injury. Three mice per group were used for scRNA-seq, and group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test, or the Kruskal-Wallis test with D
papers.summary: This study used single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse midbrain to characterize how sub-acute atrazine exposure alters dopaminergic neurons. The authors identify autophagy-associated transcriptional changes that may render dopaminergic neurons vulnerable to injury, highlighting cell-type-specific neurotoxic responses to the herbicide.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, and shows that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, including coexisting oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'dynamical zoo' of behaviors, assess robustness, and classify emergent dynamics. The work challenges the traditional separation of multistability and oscillations in gene regulatory network studies.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: The authors present scRICH, a computational framework that infers cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data while accounting for heterogeneity across individual cells. It aims to reveal how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions, addressing a gap in existing inference methods that often ignore cell-level variability.

papers.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
papers.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. These f
papers.summary: This review argues that Ehrlich carcinoma and its ascitic form, long used mainly for anticancer drug screening, are underappreciated models for studying aggressive tumor biology, including angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and therapy resistance. The authors propose integrating these classical models with modern systems biology approaches to better align them with precision oncology research.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that host-like temperature (37°C) enables pathogenic Leptospira to take up and metabolize glucose, contrary to the long-held view that this bacterium relies mainly on fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors introduce MNRS, a computational method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies that could overcome primary non-response to targeted drugs. By identifying drug pairs whose combined effects best mitigate non-response signatures, the approach offers a systems-biology framework for narrowing the vast space of possible combinations.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: The authors present a computational framework that combines machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how gut microbes, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, alter tumor metabolic networks and drug responses in colorectal cancer. By learning metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles, the model predicts synergistic drug combinations that account for microbiome composition. This provides a new approach for designing microbiome-aware combination therapies.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc), using transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data, and spatial assays. The authors present a rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat, supported by molecular dynamics simulations. The work emphasizes donor-resolved inference to identify fibroblast states relevant to SSc pathology.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational 'backtracing' strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to identify host proteins whose metabolic activity supports bacterial survival. They predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb growth and validated these predictions through pharmacological inhibition, linking host metabolic perturbations to specific Mtb proteins.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian rhythm regulators to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By combining compound perturbation profiles and pharmacological bioactivity data, the authors identify existing drugs that may target both AD pathology and circadian disruption. The work highlights circadian biology as an under-explored axis for AD therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: MetworkPy: A Python Package for Graph- and Information-theoretic Investigation of Metabolic Networks.
papers.abstract: Metabolism plays an important role in physiology and disease. In silico Genome-Scale Metabolic Models (GSMMs) are useful for informing analysis of metabolism and contextualizing high-throughput molecular profiling data. Flux balance analysis (FBA) based approaches can use GSMMs to predict metabolic reaction flux states and condition-specific alterations, but most FBA methods are limited by: 1) needing metabolic objective functions that are difficult to define experimentally, and 2) confining comparisons to extrema of reaction flux distributions.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MetworkPy is a new Python package that analyzes genome-scale metabolic models using graph theory and information theory, avoiding the need for predefined metabolic objective functions that limit traditional flux balance analysis. It enables comparison of full reaction flux distributions rather than just their extremes, providing a more flexible framework for contextualizing metabolic profiling data.

papers.title: Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction to Decipher the Molecular Mechanisms Governing Bacteriocyte-Based Symbioses.
papers.abstract: Intracellular bacteria with beneficial roles for their hosts are present in more than 10% of all insect species. In intracellular nutritional symbioses, these symbionts are typically confined to specialized host cells known as bacteriocytes. Bacteriocytes are remarkable novel cells that arose independently and repeatedly across multiple insect lineages. They are fascinating structures, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating their development, function and even their evolutionary origins, remain largely unknown. Nonetheless, an important role for certain transcription factors in development an
papers.summary: This review discusses how gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction can be used to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying bacteriocyte-based nutritional symbioses in insects. Bacteriocytes are specialized host cells that house beneficial intracellular bacteria and evolved independently multiple times across insect lineages, yet their developmental and functional regulation remains poorly understood. The authors highlight the role of transcription factors in bacteriocyte development and argue that GRN reconstruction offers a promising framework for uncovering these mechanisms and their evolutionary origins.

papers.title: Whole-cell spatiotemporal model and multimodal data illuminate the multiscale light responses in a photosynthetic bacterium.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central carbon metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subcellular organi
papers.summary: The authors built a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents subcellular spatial organization and integrates processes across timescales, from fast redox-dependent post-translational modifications to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. By combining this model with multimodal data, they dissect the multiscale regulatory dynamics underlying light and energy adaptation across diel cycles. The work demonstrates how whole-cell spatiotemporal modeling can unify disparate regulatory layers to explain photosynthetic adaptation.

papers.title: Homeostatic Correction During Severe Physiologic Stress: A Phase-Specific Model for GC-GRα-Coordinated Organism-Wide Adaptation.
papers.abstract: Critical illness is increasingly recognized as a disorder of disrupted systemic homeostasis rather than simply a consequence of maladaptive systemic inflammation or isolated organ failure. Although researchers have extensively investigated adaptive biologic responses to severe physiologic stress, far less attention has been paid to the integrative mechanisms that coordinate these responses across multiple organ systems throughout the course of illness. This review synthesizes current evidence from systems biology, immunology, endocrinology, network physiology, and critical care to present a sy
papers.summary: This review proposes a phase-specific model in which glucocorticoids and the glucocorticoid receptor alpha (GC-GRα) coordinate organism-wide homeostatic correction during severe physiologic stress, reframing critical illness as a disorder of disrupted systemic homeostasis rather than isolated inflammation or organ failure. It synthesizes evidence across systems biology, immunology, endocrinology, network physiology, and critical care to describe how adaptive responses are integrated across organ systems over the course of illness.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Plant Gene Regulatory Networks.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are the maps that plant biologists most want to draw, with arrows pointing from transcription factors to the genes they control, explaining how plants develop and respond to the environment. Since experimental validation of even one arrow can take years, and a single plant genome harbours tens of millions of candidate TF-target pairs, this gap has driven the development of numerous computational methods for GRN inference. Here I review three generations of computational approaches to plant GRN inference and measure them against a five-level ladder of evidence, i
papers.summary: This review traces three generations of computational methods for inferring plant gene regulatory networks, from early correlation-based approaches to modern machine learning models. It evaluates these methods against a five-level ladder of evidence strength, highlighting the gap between computational predictions and experimental validation. The paper argues that AI-driven approaches are essential given the millions of candidate transcription factor-target pairs in plant genomes that cannot be tested experimentally.

papers.title: An Integrated Biological Model for Precision Pulmonary Rehabilitation in COPD.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary rehabilitation improves symptoms, exercise capacity and quality of life in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), although patients with similar clinical characteristics often show different responses. This review summarizes the biological determinants of rehabilitation responsiveness identified through more than 10 years of translational research. Evidence from longitudinal studies of elderly patients with severe COPD undergoing standardized pulmonary rehabilitation was integrated with clinical, functional, molecular, immunological, cognitive, behavioural and lifestyle data,
papers.summary: This review synthesizes over a decade of translational research to identify biological determinants that explain why COPD patients respond differently to pulmonary rehabilitation. It proposes an integrated model combining clinical, functional, molecular, immunological, cognitive, behavioral, and lifestyle data to enable precision rehabilitation approaches.

papers.title: Rhizobia bacteroid transcription helps to coordinate the soybean nodule drought response.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. [Merr.]) nitrogen fixation is sensitive to soil drying and is an important target for improving soybean drought resilience. Transcriptional regulation of the nodule drought response and the influence of symbiotic rhizobia are not well understood. We measured whole-plant responses to mild and moderate soil moisture deficit (41% and 20% of field capacity) alongside the nodule transcriptome, including soybean and Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens transcripts, in two soybean genotypes ('Benning' and PI 471938) that were previously found to have diverging nitrogen fixation droug
papers.summary: This study examined how soybean nodules respond to mild and moderate drought at the whole-plant and transcriptome level, including both soybean and its symbiotic rhizobia (Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens) transcripts, in two genotypes with differing nitrogen fixation drought tolerance. The findings suggest that rhizobia bacteroid transcription actively contributes to coordinating the nodule drought response, rather than the plant acting alone.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: The authors present CardamomOT, a mechanistic framework that combines optimal transport with a gene regulatory network-driven model of gene expression to infer regulatory networks, reconstruct differentiation trajectories, and enable generative modeling from single-cell RNA-seq time courses. It extends their earlier CARDAMOM method by removing reliance on relative ordering of time points and improving trajectory reconstruction. The approach aims to recover causal regulator-target relationships despite the inability to directly measure protein dynamics at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Synthetic Biology and Systems Metabolic Engineering of Aminoglycoside Antibiotics: From Biosynthetic Pathways to Resistance-Evading and Low-Toxicity Design.
papers.abstract: Aminoglycoside antibiotics are important therapeutic agents in the clinical treatment of Gram-negative bacterial infections; however, the spread of antimicrobial resistance, together with dose-limiting ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity side effects, substantially restricts their clinical utility. Recent advances in synthetic biology and systems metabolic engineering have provided powerful approaches for elucidating and engineering the biosynthetic pathways of these antibiotics. This review systematically summarizes the conserved biosynthetic logic of aminoglycosides, with particular emphasis on t
papers.summary: This review examines how synthetic biology and systems metabolic engineering are being applied to aminoglycoside antibiotics, covering their conserved biosynthetic pathways and efforts to engineer new variants. The authors highlight strategies aimed at overcoming antimicrobial resistance and reducing the dose-limiting ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity that constrain clinical use.

papers.title: Selection favors cost-ordered adaptive mutational paths in a stress-magnitude-dependent manner.
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to stress requires adaptive strategies beyond canonical regulatory mechanisms. Stress varies, both qualitatively and quantitatively, across physiological niches and exerts distinct selection pressures on colonizing bacteria. Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies to withstand various stressful conditions, yet how they tailor their responses to different magnitudes of the same stressor remains poorly understood. We used multiple adaptive laboratory evolution experiments of Escherichia coli across varying paraquat concentrations and genetic backgrounds to dissect adaptive st
papers.summary: This study used adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli across different concentrations of the same stressor (paraquat) to examine how stress magnitude shapes adaptive mutational paths. The authors found that selection favors cost-ordered mutational trajectories, meaning mutations with lower fitness costs tend to be acquired first, and that this ordering depends on the magnitude of the stress. This reveals how bacteria tailor adaptive strategies to quantitative variation in stress.

papers.title: Thermo-flux: generation and analysis of thermodynamic-stoichiometric metabolic network models.
papers.abstract: Metabolic modeling with stoichiometric models and flux balance analysis (FBA) has greatly advanced our understanding of metabolism. However, valid FBA predictions require mechanistically correct constraints. Thermodynamic constraints can increase the mechanistic foundations of stoichiometric models and reduce the solution space, but incorporating them has so far required cumbersome manual effort. To circumvent manual curation, we introduce 'Thermo-Flux', a semi-automated Python package that converts stoichiometric models into comprehensive thermodynamic-stoichiometric models. 'Thermo-Flux' ena
papers.summary: Thermo-Flux is a semi-automated Python package that converts existing stoichiometric metabolic models into thermodynamic-stoichiometric models by adding thermodynamic constraints, reducing the need for manual curation. This improves the mechanistic correctness of flux balance analysis predictions and narrows the solution space, making metabolic modeling more reliable and accessible.

papers.title: From plasmid sequence to process design: A computational analysis of metabolism in the context of plasmid DNA manufacturing.
papers.abstract: Detailed understanding of plasmid-host physiological interactions and recombinant protein expression is crucial for the design and optimization of plasmid DNA (pDNA) manufacturing processes. Successfully transformed host cells carrying one or more copies of a particular plasmid exhibit modified metabolic behavior which may include reduced specific growth rate, increased metabolic resource cycling (ATP/ADP, NAD/NADH, NADP/NADPH) and, in some cases, even modified nutrient uptake and metabolite secretion rates. Mapping plasmid design features to critical process parameters (CPPs), such as specifi
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that links plasmid sequence features to host-cell metabolic behavior in order to inform the design and optimization of plasmid DNA manufacturing processes. It highlights how plasmid-bearing cells show altered growth, energy cofactor cycling, and nutrient uptake/secretion, and aims to map plasmid design features onto critical process parameters.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approaches for Biomarker and Pathway Discovery in Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma.
papers.abstract: Malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) is a highly aggressive thoracic cancer with limited treatment options and poor prognosis.
papers.summary: This paper applies integrative bioinformatics and machine learning methods to identify biomarkers and pathways in malignant pleural mesothelioma, an aggressive cancer with poor prognosis. The approach combines multi-omics data analysis with predictive modeling to uncover candidate molecular signatures. The findings may inform future diagnostic or therapeutic strategies, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific discoveries.

papers.title: Systems biology-driven drug repurposing in glioblastoma via antigen and pathway mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options and poor patient survival. This study aimed to identify key genes and altered pathways in GBM and to explore potential drug-repurposing candidates using a systems biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies a systems biology workflow to glioblastoma, integrating gene expression and pathway analysis to identify key dysregulated genes and pathways, then maps these to candidate drugs for repurposing. The authors propose antigen and pathway targets as a basis for prioritizing existing drugs that could be redirected toward GBM treatment.

papers.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: Evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species.
papers.abstract: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension. We show that in simple organisms, aging is governed by a limited number of high-leverage pathways, whereas in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems c
papers.summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework arguing that lifespan extension interventions lose effectiveness as organismal complexity increases. In simple organisms, aging is controlled by a few high-leverage pathways that can be readily manipulated, but in mammals aging emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory networks that resist single-target interventions and instead require system-level buffering. The work synthesizes comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to explain the declining ceiling of lifespan extension across species.

papers.title: Multi-omics insights into uric acid metabolism in cardiometabolic disease: from genetics to metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Hyperuricemia, characterized by elevated serum uric acid (SUA) levels, is increasingly recognized as a significant contributor to cardiometabolic diseases including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, metabolic syndrome, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. In the past, uric acid was seen mainly as a byproduct of purine metabolism linked to gout. However, growing evidence suggests that it plays an active role in causing metabolic and vascular dysfunction. Mechanistic studies have shown that higher uric acid levels can induce endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress,
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that elevated serum uric acid is not merely a gout-related byproduct but an active contributor to cardiometabolic diseases such as hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and atherosclerosis. It integrates genetic and metabolomic findings to describe mechanisms—including endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress—by which uric acid may drive metabolic and vascular damage.

papers.title: Proteomics and network biology insights into inflammation suppression during prolonged high-altitude hypoxia acclimatization.
papers.abstract: For decades, the study of high-altitude acclimatization has been a vital area of scientific inquiry aimed at enhancing human resilience, particularly in the context of military deployments. While most existing research has focused on acute inflammatory responses to hypoxia, limited information is available on the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term high-altitude acclimatization. To address this gap, the present study investigated the plasma proteomic alterations associated with 120 days of high-altitude exposure at 14,500 ft by employing quantitative proteomics combined with computationa
papers.summary: This study used quantitative plasma proteomics combined with computational network analysis to profile molecular changes during 120 days of high-altitude exposure at 14,500 ft. The key finding is that prolonged acclimatization is associated with suppression of inflammatory pathways, extending beyond the acute inflammatory responses typically studied. The work provides proteomic and network-level insights into long-term hypoxia adaptation with potential relevance to military and high-altitude operations.

papers.title: Population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie secondary metabolic diversification in Aspergillus flavus Link and the domestication of Aspergillus oryzae (Ahlb.).
papers.abstract: The genomic signatures of microbial domestication remain poorly understood within the context of natural population variation. Here, we demonstrate that Aspergillus oryzae, the filamentous fungus used in soy sauce and sake production, shares more recent ancestry with a predominantly northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C). A. oryzae isolates also overlap with the recently described, clinically enriched A. flavus population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All isolates tested retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. At the tr
papers.summary: This study shows that the domesticated fungus Aspergillus oryzae, used in soy sauce and sake production, is most closely related to a northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C), with additional overlap to a clinically enriched population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All tested isolates remained pathogenic in a zebrafish infection model, and population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie diversification of secondary metabolism. The work links natural population variation to microbial domestication signatures.

papers.title: Immunogenic cell death and tertiary lymphoid structures jointly define dysregulated antitumor immune states and therapeutic vulnerability in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study examines how immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) jointly shape antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma. By integrating these two biologically distinct but interconnected immune processes, the authors identify distinct immune states that link to prognosis and therapeutic vulnerability. The work suggests that combining ICD and TLS signatures could improve patient stratification and guide treatment decisions.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a shared human-mouse gene space using supervised contrastive learning, then predicts transcription factor–target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression relationships via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and species-specific distribution shifts in GRN inference. The work extends existing single-cell GRN methods by adding cross-species pretraining.

papers.title: An experimentally validated manually curated genome-scale metabolic model of Enterococcus faecium TX0016 reproduces high-throughput phenotyping data.
papers.abstract: Enterococci are Gram-positive opportunistic pathogens responsible for a wide range of nosocomial infections. One enterococcal species, Enterococcus faecium, is steadily increasing in prevalence and has been listed among major multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens. To gain systems-level insights into its metabolism and support discovery of potential therapeutic targets, we constructed iDR478, a comprehensive manually curated genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) for E. faecium TX0016 (strain DO). The reconstruction was based on extensive homology searches and literature evidence, and was further re
papers.summary: The authors built iDR478, a manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the multidrug-resistant pathogen Enterococcus faecium TX0016, using homology searches and literature evidence. The model was experimentally validated and reproduces high-throughput phenotyping data, providing a systems-level view of the organism's metabolism to support identification of therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Towards epigenetically informed and biobank-driven precision immunotherapy in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is a highly immunogenic and therapeutically intricate solid tumor, exemplifying the interactions between tumors and the immune system. Despite the significant enhancement in survival rates for patients with advanced melanoma due to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), numerous patients either exhibit resistance to these agents or develop immune evasion mechanisms. This underscores the pressing necessity to identify biological determinants of drug responses. A significant body of research indicates that epigenetic alterations, including DNA methylation, histone modificat
papers.summary: This review discusses how epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation and histone modifications influence melanoma's response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, and argues for integrating epigenetic data with large biobank resources to identify biomarkers of immunotherapy response. The authors highlight the need to understand biological determinants of drug resistance and immune evasion to enable more precise, personalized immunotherapy for melanoma patients.
